subject: saving compiled stan models in R

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: saving compiled stan models in R
parts:
This raises an interesting issue.  We will soon have Stan emulators for lm, glm, lmer, blmer, etc.  These will have some precompiled Stan models.  We'd like to do the precompiling when installing the package (stan_lm, etc., or whatever we want to call these packages) into R, and then have these precompiled models available for running.
A


On Jul 14, 2013, at 8:29 PM, Jiqiang Guo wrote:

As Ben pointed out, you can first try not to use R.cache package, which is not necessary at all when using RStan.  Sampling can always be done for a compiled model with different data and other inputs so compiling is needed just once for the same model.  

And I am afraid that the problem is that R.cache does not handle objects created in RStan, which has a dynamic shared object created from compiling the C++ code.  From the description, I guess that after the dynamic shared object was unloaded by R (this happens automatically by R at a time that is not determined by the user), R.cache cannot load the dynamic shared object and thus a segfault follows.  

--
Jiqiang 

--

parts:

Ben

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: saving compiled stan models in R
parts:
I think Andrew just wants to cut out the compile time for
common models that we could distribute with
the more general package.

We could, instead, write an R package just for these
models. That would be easy to get onto CRAN because we
don't need the C++ libs or long compile times that are
currently preventing RStan from being accepted for CRAN.

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: saving compiled stan models in R
parts:
On Monday, July 15, 2013 11:42:50 AM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
I think Andrew just wants to cut out the compile time for
common models that we could distribute with
the more general package.
Me too, that is why I am aiming for 1 .stan file per R function we are emulating. I just don't know if it is going to be fast enough with lme4() because we don't have sparse matrix operations yet.

We could, instead, write an R package just for these
models.  That would be easy to get onto CRAN because we
don't need the C++ libs or long compile times that are
currently preventing RStan from being accepted for CRAN.

Not that easy, since the package in question currently depends on Stan and CRAN packages have to satisfy their dependencies via CRAN.

Ben
